title: My reality TV game runs 10+ AI contestants on whatever local model you pick, and it's turned into a weird model benchmark
author: swirllyman
selftext:
Solo dev here. Villa de Drama is a reality TV sim where ten contestants live in a villa and every line they say is generated on your own PC through llama.cpp. No API, no server.

The part I didn't expect to love is the model picker. There are 12 built in, from SmolLM2 360M up to Qwen 3 4B, and you can paste in any GGUF from Hugging Face. Same cast, same villa, different brain. Llama 3.2 1B is the default and it's pretty decent for starting, but small models and big models can really make a big difference. The game works almost like a litmus test for model testing.

The model only writes the lines. The game tracks who likes who, grudges, gossip and who's voting for who, and hands each contestant a goal before every chat. Small models can't hold a whole season in their head, but they can play one scene if you tell them what's at stake.

Voices are local too: Chatterbox, falling back to Kokoro, and gibberish if neither can keep up.

Biggest lesson so far: my test suite scored lines on how natural they sounded, and polite boring lines score great on that. Someone on Reddit called a clip "the most lifeless dialogue I've ever heard" and they were right. Now I score for whether a line would make you laugh or gasp.

Has anyone found a small model that's actually good at being a bit more snippy? Which one should I put through a season next?
